2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 10-11-2022 at about 7:00 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding on a motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-L-5476 as a pillion rider, on Tumkur-Bengaluru NH-48 road.
The said motorcycle was ridden by one Chethan in rash and negligent manner,
endangering to human life, without observing the traffic rules and regulations.
While so proceeding, at Kuluvanahalli 'U' turn, they were crossing the road towards Lakkenahalli side.

At that time, suddenly the rider of Hero Splendor Motorcycle Venkatesh vs Thimmegowda on 1 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100673821/

sentences.text:
At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-L- 5476 and Hero Splendor Motorcycle bearing Engine No.JA07ABM9B00645, Chassis No.MBLJAW187M9B00660 in the said accident,
issuance of insurance policy by the respondents No.2 and 4 in respect of both the vehicles and its validity as on the date of accident
, are not in dispute.

Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owners of both the offending vehicles/Respondents No.1 and 3, as they did not choose to appear and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.2 and 4 insurance companies have denied the above stated facts and circumstances of the accident and have taken specific defence that, there is no negligence on the part of the riders of their respective insured vehicles and the said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of their respective opposite vehicle.
But, they have failed to establish the said contentions.

Except, the self serving statements of R.W.1 and R.W.2, who are the representatives of the respondent No.2 and 4 insurance companies, there is absolutely no other oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondents No.2 & 4 to show that, the said accident has taken place due to sole negligence on the part of the riders of their respective opposite motorcycle.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the riders of both the offending vehicles and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
It clearly goes to show that, the riders of both the vehicles have equally contributed in the cause of accident.

14. Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazar also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place at the middle of 26 feet wide Tumakuru-Bengaluru NH-48 road, at Kuluvanahalli 'U' turn, due to collusion of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-L-5476 and Hero Splendor Motorcycle bearing Engine No.JA07ABM9B00645, Chassis No.MBLJAW187M9B00660 .
Further, as per the Ex.P.5 Motor Vehicle Accident Report, the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-L-5476 and Hero Splendor Motorcycle bearing Engine No.JA07ABM9B00645, Chassis No.MBLJAW187M9B00660, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the riders of both the offending vehicles.

Further, the investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.6, has also clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent riding of the riders of both the offending vehicles i.e. motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-52-L- 5476 and Hero Splendor Motorcycle bearing Engine No.JA07ABM9B00645, Chassis No.MBLJAW187M9B00660.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the owners or the riders of said offending vehicles.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicles in the accident, rash and negligent riding of the riders of both the offending vehicles and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

15. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.4 wound certificate, Ex.P.7 discharge summary,
Ex.P.12 and 14 OPD records and Ex.P.13 and 15 x-rays, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in the said road traffic accident.

The petitioner has suffered right condylar Venkatesh vs Thimmegowda on 1 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100673821/
6 fracture and left body fracture of mandible, communited depress fracture left intertrochanteric and subtrochanteric region of femur, communited depress fracture frontal bone, orbit roof fracture bilateral and other injuries.
he same is deposed by P.W.2 and P.W.3, who are the doctors who have clinically examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability.

On the other hand,
there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondents to show that, the above medical records are false documents.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondents No.2 and 4 have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent riding of the riders of both the offending vehicles and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the said accident.

16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

19. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the riders of both the offending vehicles i.e. motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-L-5476 and Hero Splendor Motorcycle bearing Engine No.JA07ABM9B00645, Chassis No.MBLJAW187M9B00660 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that,
the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to Venkatesh vs Thimmegowda on 1 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100673821/

To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.11.
As per Ex.P.11, the date of birth of the petitioner is 30-06-1988.
The accident has taken place on 10-11-2022 at about 7:00 p.m.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 34 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered right condylar fracture and left body fracture of mandible, communited depress fracture left intertrochanteric and subtrochanteric region of femur, communited depress fracture frontal bone, orbit roof fracture bilateral.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, there is 45% permanent physical disability for left lower limb and 22.5% of whole body of the petitioner.

Further, the Ex.P.4 wound certificate, Ex.P.7 discharge summary, Ex.P.12 and 14 OPD records and Ex.P.13 and 15 x-rays clearly speaks that,
the petitioner has suffered the above stated injuries and he has undergone surgery for the said injuries.
Though, the learned counsel for respondents No.2 and 4 have cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, there is no disability to the petitioner and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 10-11-2022 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 23-05- 2024, which is after lapse of one year and six months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.

Further, it is pertinent to note that,
P.W.2 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, fracture is mal-united, the implants are in situ, the treatment to the petitioner is completed, he has not advised any treatment for mal-union of the fracture and the petitioner can do day to day activities with difficulties.

Further, the P.W.3, who is the doctor, said to have examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability suffered by him due to facial and orthopedic injuries, has deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner had suffered fracture of left body of mandible, fracture of right condylar & bilateral orbit fracture and depressed frontal bone and for the said injuries he has undergone surgery.

Further deposed that, on clinically and radiological examination of the injuries sustained by the petitioner,
he found that, the petitioner has suffered 13% disability to the whole body in respect of facial injuries.
But, during his cross-examination he has clearly admitted that, the injuries sustained by the petitioner are totally cured and there is no need of any further treatment to the petitioner.

But,
both P.W.2 & P.W.3 have deposed in their evidence that, the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

sentences.text: a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as agriculturist and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondent No.2 and 4 have specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before the accident he was working as agriculturist and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.

Therefore, in such circumstances,
there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2022.

Hence,
the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,86,000/-.
b) As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 34 years is 16.

Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,86,000 X 15/100 X 16 = Rs.4,46,400/-.
ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.5,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 33 medical bills, as per Ex.P.8.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.3,30,145/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,30,145/- under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:

In the present case, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e. right condylar fracture and left body fracture of mandible, communited depress fracture left intertrochanteric and subtrochanteric region of femur, communited depress fracture frontal bone,
orbit roof fracture bilateral.
As per Ex.P.7 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 8 days from 10-11-2022 to 17-11-2022, in V.P. Magnus Hospital, Bengaluru.

Further,
as per P.W.2 and P.W.3, the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.60,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:
As per Ex.P.7 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 8 days in V.P. Magnus Hospital, Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.

is awarded towards the attendant charges.

He might have spent considerable amount towards food and nourishment during that period.

Therefore, compensation of Rs.800 x 8 =

sentences.text: vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Kuluvanahalli, Lakkenahalli, Bengaluru Rural, the accident has taken place on Tumkuru-Bengaluru NH-48 road, at Kuluvanahalli 'U' turn and the petitioner has taken treatment at V.P. Magnus Hospital, Bengaluru.
Taking into consideration the distance in between the above places, compensation of Rs.5,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 8 days as in-patient at V.P. Magnus Hospital, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries sustained by him.
He might have taken rest for about 3 months and lost his income for the said period.
Therefore, Rs.15,500 x 3 = Rs.46,500/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 34 years and unfortunately he has suffered right distal humerus comminuted fracture with radial nerve injury.
Further, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 15% to the whole body.
